texts.text: Lighthouses were once staffed by keepers who trimmed wicks, wound clockwork, and logged every passing ship through long winter nights. Automation arrived gradually: electric lamps replaced oil, rotating lenses were driven by motors instead of weights, and remote monitoring made resident crews unnecessary. Many towers now serve as museums, while their modern successors are small solar-powered beacons mounted on steel frames. Mariners still rely on the characteristic flash pattern of each light to fix their position when satellite navigation fails, which is why authorities publish detailed light lists every year.
